title: Melanoma Brain Metastasis Mouse Model for Drug Testing
author: Almazan, Turapov, et al.
materials: HBSS, calcium, magnesium, no phenol red
IVIS spectrum in vivo imaging system

Timing: 1–3 days
1.Thaw the GFP and luciferase-expressing YUMM3.2;Pten−/−;Akt1E17K melanoma cells and culture them in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM)/F-12 supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin, and 1% Minimum Essential Medium (MEM) Non-Essential Amino Acids Solution in a 10 cm tissue culture dish.2.Maintain cells in culture at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 1–3 days.3.Prepare for the injection when the preferred confluency is achieved.4.Using a fluorescence microscope, confirm the presence of GFP expression in the cells as shown in Figure 1. Successful GFP expression also confirms the presence of luciferase in the cell line, which is crucial in the upcoming steps of the protocol. Furthermore, a luciferase assay may be performed to confirm luciferase activity in the cell line.Figure 1GFP expression in the YUMM3.2;Pten−/−;Akt1E17K melanoma cells(A and B) Using a fluorescence microscope, GFP expression is confirmed in the cell line (A) with the GFP filter (B).
Note: We recommend achieving approximately 80% cell confluency prior to cell injection, as over confluency can compromise the viability of the cells.

steps.title: Culture melanoma cells to confluency
steps.instruction: Thaw GFP‑ and luciferase‑expressing YUMM3.2;Pten−/−;Akt1E17K melanoma cells and grow them in DMEM/F‑12 supplemented with 10 % FBS, 1 % Penicillin‑Streptomycin, and 1 % MEM Non‑Essential Amino Acids in a 10 cm dish at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 1–3 days until ~80 % confluency is reached; confirm GFP expression by fluorescence microscopy (luciferase activity may also be verified).

substeps.instruction: Thaw the cells and plate them in a 10 cm tissue‑culture dish containing DMEM/F‑12 + 10 % FBS, 1 % Pen‑Strep, 1 % MEM NEAA.
Incubate at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ for 1–3 days, monitoring growth.
When cells reach approximately 80 % confluency (recommended), proceed to injection preparation.
Examine cells under a fluorescence microscope to verify GFP expression; optionally perform a luciferase assay to confirm luciferase activity.

steps.title: Prepare cells for intracranial injection
steps.instruction: Harvest ~80 % confluent melanoma cells, determine live cell concentration, calculate the volume needed for 30 cells per newborn mouse, and resuspend the calculated cell number in a final volume of 10 mL 1× HBSS, keeping the suspension on ice until injection.

substeps.instruction: Remove media from the 10 cm dish by gentle aspiration.
Wash cells once with 1× PBS.
Add 1 mL 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA, swirl to cover cells, and incubate at 37 °C for 5–7 min.
Check under a microscope that all cells have detached; ensure complete detachment before proceeding.
Add 5 mL fresh media to neutralize trypsin, rinse the dish several times to collect all cells, and transfer the suspension to a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge 4 min at 400 × g at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant gently and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL fresh media.
Add 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue to a sterile microcentrifuge tube, mix 10 µL of the cell suspension with the stain, and load 10 µL of this mixture into a Countess II counting chamber.
Run the Countess II Automated Cell Counter, record the live cell concentration (alternative: manual hemocytometer count).
Calculate the volume required to deliver 30 cells per mouse, aiming for a final suspension of 10 mL at 10 cells/µL (e.g., if concentration = 8.67 × 10⁶ cells/mL, 3 µL contains 30 cells).
Transfer the calculated cell volume into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and add 100 µL 1× HBSS; resuspend gently.
Move the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube containing ~5–10 mL 1× HBSS and spin 2 min at 450 g at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 100 µL 1× HBSS.
Add another ~5–10 mL 1× HBSS and repeat the spin as above.
Aspirate supernatant, resuspend pellet in 100 µL 1× HBSS, then combine with 9 900 µL 1× HBSS in a 15 mL tube; vortex and invert to mix.
Aliquot 5 mL of the cell suspension into a clean 5 mL Eppendorf tube and place on ice.
Prepare two 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes: one containing 1 mL 1× HBSS and the other containing 1 mL 70 % ethanol for downstream steps.

description: Melanoma is one of the deadliest forms of skin cancer, with brain metastases being the major cause of treatment failure.2 To address this issue and evaluate the effects of drug treatments on established brain metastases, this protocol outlines the steps for generating a murine model of melanoma brain metastases using GFP and luciferase-expressing syngeneic YUMM3.2;Pten−/−;Akt1E17K melanoma cells in newborn “glowing head” C57BL/6 mice.1 The expression of GFP in this modified cell line has the advantage of confirming delivery of the virus harboring AKT1E17K and luciferase, with the latter being essential for the bioluminescent imaging (BLI) technique. Additionally, this cell line expresses BRAFV600E, which activates the MAPK pathway, and expresses AKT1E17K in the context of Cdkn2a and Pten loss, resulting in activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, which is a common occurrence in human melanoma. Furthermore, we have previously demonstrated that PI3K/AKT pathway activation in this context is required for melanoma cell growth in the brain.3 This protocol also takes advantage of the immunocompetent “glowing head” C57BL/6 mice engineered by Day et al., as this mouse strain is tolerized to both GFP and luciferase.4 Additionally, the albino phenotype of these mice reduces the effects of autofluorescence. For this model, we intracranially inject 30 YUMM3.2;Pten−/−;Akt1E17K melanoma cells into newborn mice, as previous pilot studies with injections of 1000 and 100 cells resulted in early mortality, thus prompting the use of a smaller number of cells. Furthermore, newborn mice are utilized because their skull is softer and injections can be done with a gas tight Hamilton syringe without the need for a stereotactic injection device. Lastly, bioluminescent imaging will be used to detect the establishment and colonization of the cell line in the brain, as well as monitor tumor burden over time. Various models have been developed to study melanoma, including zebrafish models
